first_impression.reaction: Emma's torn between the two, so this is exactly what I wanted. 'A choice between two settings, not two standards' is a sensible way to start; nobody's selling me a sunset yet. I'll read it properly, top to bottom, and see what it says about getting Mum there.

journey.quote: Both islands have their own airport, and Smartraveller warns that ferries can be delayed or cancelled in strong winds, so guests should plan their arrival with time to spare.
journey.reaction: Good. Smartraveller up near the top, and a plain warning about ferries. That tells me they aren't hiding the awkward bits.

journey.section: Santorini or Mykonos for your wedding: the short answer
journey.quote: Neither island wins. They answer different questions.
journey.reaction: Fair enough. I'd rather be told how to choose than be told what to choose. I can sit with Emma and go through it.

journey.section: Santorini vs Mykonos at a glance
journey.quote: The same seven questions, answered for each island. This is a comparison, not a ranking.
journey.reaction: A table I can show my husband. It fits on the iPad if I turn it sideways. The 'Season' row saying Naxos threw me for a second until I read further down.

journey.quote: Hamlets spread across the rim of the caldera, so most ceremony spaces look west and down, over water, to the volcanic islands.
journey.reaction: Lovely for the photos, but 'down' and 'on the rim of a cliff' makes me think of steps. Lots of them. Mum uses a walking frame. Nothing in the venue section tells me which of these places she could actually get around.

journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is your single point of contact, one person start to finish, and confirms each venue's inclusions in writing before you commit
journey.reaction: One person, and in writing before we commit. That's the accountability I want for this sort of money. I'd like them to confirm access for older guests in writing too.

journey.quote: Mykonos Grand states that both partners must be Christian Orthodox for a religious wedding on the hotel premises.
journey.reaction: Now that's the kind of thing you find out far too late. Glad it's spelled out. Emma's fiancé isn't Orthodox, so that's useful straight away.

journey.quote: Katikies has Santorini properties in Oia, Imerovigli and Fira, and lists weddings and hotel takeovers among its event types.
journey.reaction: By the second list of hotel names I was skimming. Emma will care about these; I just want to know which ones are safe and sensible.

journey.section: Getting your guests there: Santorini Airport
journey.quote: The airport has Schengen and non-Schengen departure areas, public bus and taxi services, and an Accessible Travel section for passengers with reduced mobility.
journey.reaction: Reduced mobility mentioned at the airport. Good. At least someone thought about it.

journey.section: Getting your guests there: By sea
journey.quote: In most cases passengers carry their own luggage up and down stairs, and some services lack suitable access for people with disabilities.
journey.reaction: Honest, and a bit alarming. So Mum flies, full stop. I appreciate being told rather than finding out on the dock.

journey.section: Getting your guests there: By sea
journey.quote: Older relatives and anyone with limited mobility are worth planning around on either island.
journey.reaction: Yes, thank you. But 'worth planning around' and then nothing more. Who does the planning? Is that the Advisor's job or ours?

journey.section: When to marry on each island
journey.quote: Naxos is the nearest listed station to both, so the figures below apply to either island and are labelled as Naxos.
journey.reaction: It's explained, and I respect that they didn't make up numbers. July at 27 degrees with no rain looks fine on paper, but the heatwave line underneath is what I'll remember.

journey.quote: Smartraveller also notes that Greece sits in an active seismic zone, with earthquakes and volcanic activity near major destinations including Santorini, and advises following local authorities.
journey.reaction: Earthquakes and a live volcano. Good that they say it, but it gives me a fright, and there's not a word about travel insurance for the older ones, which is the first thing I'd ring about.

journey.section: Getting legally married on either island, in brief
journey.quote: For the Greek civil steps on each island, check with the municipality and the Australian Embassy in Athens, including any fees.
journey.reaction: Check with the municipality? In Greek? Is Emma meant to do that herself, or does the Advisor or the venue help? I can't tell who handles the paperwork if she books through you.

journey.section: Santorini or Mykonos wedding questions, answered
journey.quote: Several venues publish wedding brochures or packages, including Canaves, Santa Marina and Grand Ambassador, and your inclusions should be set out in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: In writing again. That's what I want to hear on the money question.

journey.section: Choose your island with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: The fee is agreed in writing before any work begins, and inclusions are confirmed in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: One person, our time zone, AUD, fee in writing. That's the paragraph I'll forward to my husband. I'd still want a phone call before a cent goes anywhere.

unanswered_questions: Which of these venues can a guest with a walking frame get around, from room to ceremony spot to reception? The Santorini cliff-top ones especially.
When the page says older relatives are 'worth planning around', does the Wedded Advisor do that planning, or is it left to us?
What travel and medical insurance should older guests have, given the heat, wildfire and earthquake warnings?
Who does the Greek civil paperwork in practice if we book through Wedded Concierge: my daughter, the venue or the Wedded Advisor?
Is the deposit protected, and who reads a contract written in Greek and in euros?
Who do I ring if something goes wrong at 2am Greek time?
Is the first step a phone call with a real person, before anything is booked or paid?
would_share_with: My husband, with the comparison table and the closing paragraph (one person, AUD, fee in writing)
My daughter, with the Mykonos Grand Orthodox rule and the ferry and heat warnings
My sister, who'll travel with Mum, with the ferry stairs and airport accessibility lines

cta_reaction.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is one person, start to finish, who works in your time zone and quotes in AUD for Australian couples.
cta_reaction.why: It ticks most of my boxes: a person, our time zone, AUD and the fee in writing. I'd click if I knew a real person rings me first, and that they'd check which venues Mum can manage and help with the Greek paperwork.

top_3_changes: In the venue section, add one plain line that cliff-top caldera venues can mean steps and slopes, and that step-free access for older guests is something the Wedded Advisor checks with each venue in writing. The ferry section raises mobility, but the venues never do.

After 'Older relatives and anyone with limited mobility are worth planning around on either island', say who does that planning, and add one line next to the heat, wildfire and earthquake advice telling families to arrange travel and medical insurance that suits older guests.
After 'check with the municipality and the Australian Embassy in Athens', add one sentence on who handles the Greek civil paperwork in practice (the couple, with the Advisor's or venue's help).

checks.check: Every journey point and CTA reaction has an exact quote from the draft
Stayed in character as Margaret (funding parent, practical, reads top to bottom on an iPad, sent the link by her daughter)
No invented brand facts; missing business details listed as unanswered questions
HTML comments, image slots and VERIFY markers treated as invisible

Deferred business details (fees, deposits, contracts, on-the-ground contact, call first) and transfers not raised as must-fix; absent prices, absent best month, no-winner framing and sourcing not raised as problems, per orchestrator

Journey types limited to the allowed enum; turn_offs_found empty because no persona turn-off was genuinely triggered (no slang or influencer tone, paragraphs short, responsibility covered by the Wedded Advisor lines)

open_questions.question: The draft raises mobility for older guests in the ferry section but never at the cliff-top venues, which is this persona's top practical worry. Treat as should-fix? Insurance and who handles the Greek civil paperwork are smaller gaps. Deposit protection, contract language, 2am contact and call-first are deferred business details.

assumptions: Margaret reads the whole article on an iPad because her daughter sent it, and her own mother uses a walking frame (per voice samples).
Prices, a best month and an island verdict are deliberately absent, so their absence was not raised.
